key_insight: A differentiable JAX finite-element solver combines large-deformation shells and contact to simulate patient-specific aortic valves with 5.3–6.5× GPU speedups over corresponding CPU runs.
engineering_relevance: Faster valve mechanics simulations could support assessment of tissue properties and geometry, with future potential for gradient-based parameter identification and intervention planning.
method: Energy-based finite-strain extensible-director shells with hyperelastic materials and finite-range repulsive contact.
Regularized matrix-free Newton–Krylov equilibrium solver with two-level preconditioning.
Automatic differentiation for tangent-vector products and GPU-parallel element and quadrature computations.
evidence_signal: Component benchmarks and contact-free plate sensitivity checks supported verification; three patient-specific valves reached relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4 with median GPU runtimes of approximately 15–25 minutes.
watch_item: Sensitivity agreement was demonstrated only for a contact-free plate, leaving gradient reliability under evolving valve contact unestablished.
paper_title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
